summary: Full-extraction pass on 20 documents: IRS Whistleblower Office reports to Congress FY2010-FY2024, the 2008 first report and the FY2025 sequestration notice, plus three NHTSA documents (first-award press release, award order 2021-0001, 2024 final rule). The IRS reports had their headline tables extracted already; this pass added the full breakdowns (open claims by status/phase, days in status, closures by year of receipt and percentage, receipts by operating division, referrals to examination, monthly claim numbers, processing-time splits, TFA notices, hotline calls), restated rules and missing events. Proposed indicators: tips_share, claims_time_in_status, preliminary_award_letters, notices_to_whistleblowers. 18 documents complete, 2 partial (FY2023, FY2024 chart images).

observations.location: PDF p. 7 (printed 7), Determination of Whistleblower Award
observations.quote: the maximum allowable thirty percent (30%) of the $81 million in civil penalties that have been collected by the United States
observations.notes: Civil penalties collected under the Hyundai and Kia consent orders of 23 Nov 2020 (paid January 2021): the Non-Deferred Amounts, Hyundai $54 million + Kia $27 million = $81 million (adds up).

events.title: Notice 2008-4: initial guidance on submitting information
events.description: IRS Notice 2008-4 and a revised Form 211 give initial guidance on how to submit whistleblower information and the criteria for section 7623(b).
events.quote: The IRS issued Notice 2008-4 on December 19, 2007 to provide initial guidance on how to submit information to the IRS.

events.title: New case management system for whistleblower claims
events.description: The IRS begins recording all new section 7623 claims in a new case management system; legacy data loaded in July 2010.
events.quote: In January 2009, the IRS began using a new case management system based on commercial-off-the-shelf technology to record all new section 7623 claims.

events.title: Whistleblower Office staff increase to 21 authorised
events.description: After reviewing intake and expected workload, the IRS authorises raising Whistleblower Office staff from 17 to 21.
events.quote: the IRS authorized a staff increase to 21 in August 2010.

events.title: NHTSA opens Theta II recall-query investigations of Hyundai and Kia
events.description: Acting in part on the whistleblower's information, NHTSA opens investigations RQ17-003 (Kia) and RQ17-004 (Hyundai) into the timeliness and scope of Theta II engine recalls.
events.quote: NHTSA opened two investigations, RQ17- 003 and RQ17-004, on May 18, 2017, to probe the scope and timeliness of Hyundai and Kia's Theta II recalls.

events.title: Consent orders with Hyundai and Kia ($210 million in civil penalties)
events.description: NHTSA enters consent orders with Hyundai Motor America and Kia Motors America over untimely Theta II engine recalls and inaccurate reporting; $81 million paid in cash, the rest deferred or performance obligations.
events.quote: On November 23, 2020, the Agency entered into a Consent Order with Hyundai Motor America

events.title: Public hearing on proposed "collected proceeds" regulation
events.description: Public hearing on the January 2011 proposed regulation defining collected proceeds; final regulation issued 22 Feb 2012.
events.quote: A public hearing on the proposed regulation was held on May 11, 2011.

events.title: Final regulations on contracts with whistleblowers (section 6103(n))
events.description: Final regulations on contracts for services with whistleblowers, and the disclosure of taxpayer information under them, take effect.
events.quote: Final regulations governing the use of contracts for services related to the detection of violations of the internal revenue laws or related statutes were published and became ... effective on March 15, 2011.

events.title: GAO report on the Whistleblower Office
events.description: GAO reviews the Whistleblower Office and recommends better case data to track aging claims; the IRS generally agrees.
events.quote: In August 2011, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) published a report on its review of the Whistleblower Office.

events.title: Tax Court proposes rules to protect taxpayer information in whistleblower cases
events.description: Proposed Tax Court rules to protect taxpayer information, and in some cases the whistleblower's identity, in whistleblower award appeals.
events.quote: On December 28, 2011, the Tax Court proposed rules to require protection of taxpayer information in Tax Court proceedings

events.title: Authority to approve 7623(a) awards delegated to the Whistleblower Office Director
events.description: The IRS delegates approval of discretionary section 7623(a) awards to the Director of the Whistleblower Office.
events.quote: In 2008, the IRS delegated authority to approve 7623(a) awards to the Director of the Whistleblower Office

events.title: Informant Claims Examination unit moves into the Whistleblower Office
events.description: SB/SE transfers the 13-person ICE unit, which handles discretionary 7623(a) claims, to the Whistleblower Office; office staff reaches 36 by the end of FY2012.
events.quote: In January 2012, the Small Business/Self-Employed (SB/SE) Division transferred the Informant Claims Examination (ICE) Unit to the Whistleblower Office.

events.title: Deputy Commissioner memo sets performance objectives for whistleblower claims
events.description: Memorandum to division heads on the value of whistleblower information, timely evaluation, debriefings, and performance objectives for evaluations and award determinations.
events.quote: On June 20, 2012, the Deputy Commissioner for Services and Enforcement issued a memorandum to the Operating Division Commissioners

events.title: Proposed comprehensive section 7623 regulations
events.description: Notice of Proposed Rulemaking: framework for receipt of submissions, evaluation of contribution, and award determination and payment; comments due 19 Feb 2013.
events.quote: On December 18, 2012, a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking was published in the Federal Register.

events.title: Public hearing on proposed section 7623 regulations
events.description: Hearing on the December 2012 proposed regulations after written comments to 19 Feb 2013; final rules expected in the second quarter of FY2014.
events.quote: Written public comments were submitted through February 19, 2013, followed by a hearing on April 10, 2013.

events.title: Whistleblower Office notice on sequestration of awards
events.description: Notice that awards paid from 1 March 2013 are cut by sequestration (8.7 percent).
events.quote: In April 2013, the Whistleblower Office issued a notice regarding the impact of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, as amended.

events.title: Initial claim evaluation unit moves to SB/SE
events.description: The Initial Claim Evaluation (ICE) unit is realigned from the Whistleblower Office to the Small Business/Self-Employed Division, following Lean Six Sigma and GAO recommendations; office staff falls from 61 to 37.
events.quote: Employed (SB/SE) organization on July 10, 2016.

events.title: Deputy Commissioner memo on debriefing whistleblowers
events.description: Memorandum highlighting the value of whistleblower information and urging debriefings of whistleblowers to understand the issues.
events.quote: the Deputy Commissioner for Services and Enforcement issued a memorandum, on August 4, 2017, highlighting the value of whistleblower information

events.title: IRS and TTB memorandum on whistleblower claims
events.description: Memorandum of Understanding with the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau sets procedures for whistleblower award claims under internal revenue laws that TTB administers (announced 11 Dec 2019).
events.quote: The IRS and TTB signed a Memorandum of Understanding on December 3, 2019, making these new procedures possible.

events.title: First IRS Whistleblower Program Forum
events.description: The Whistleblower Office holds its first Whistleblower Program Forum with industry representatives.
events.quote: On April 30, 2020, the Whistleblower Office held its first ever Whistleblower Program Forum.

events.title: COVID-19 suspends intake and award issuance
events.description: Office closures delay intake of new Form 211 submissions by two and a half months; award issuance suspended for a month; in-person reviews of claim files suspended indefinitely. Month approximate (the report gives durations, not dates; mail processing resumed in June 2020).
events.quote: Processing of new Form 211 submissions (intake) was delayed two and a half months

events.title: First Whistleblower Round Table Discussion
events.description: The Whistleblower Office holds its first round table with industry representatives.
events.quote: On June 10, 2021, the Whistleblower Office held its first ever Whistleblower Round Table Discussion.

events.title: Whistleblower Office reorganised
events.description: Reorganisation creates a Deputy Director, a Quality Assurance and Data Reporting group and a Litigation Monitoring and Notification team; staff of 41.
events.quote: On July 18, 2021 the Whistleblower Office underwent a reorganization to better serve whistleblowers and to accommodate program growth.

events.title: NDAA 2021 creates overlapping FinCEN award for FBAR penalties
events.description: The IRS notes that the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act (section 6314) rewrote the FinCEN whistleblower statute (31 U.S.C. 5323), which, like IRC 7623 since 2018, authorises awards for FBAR penalties.
events.location: PDF p. 8, Legislative changes resulting in overlapping whistleblower statutes
events.quote: In January 2021, Congress passed the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for FY 2021 (NDAA 2021).

events.title: IRS Whistleblower Summit
events.description: Formal summit at IRS headquarters with the whistleblower community and IRS business units, opened by the IRS Commissioner.
events.quote: A formal Whistleblower Summit was held on October 20, 2022, at IRS headquarters

events.title: Tax Court widens disclosure to whistleblowers (Whistleblower 972-17W)
events.description: In Whistleblower 972-17W v. Commissioner, 159 T.C. No. 1 (2022), the Tax Court held that IRC 6103(h)(4)(A) allows disclosure of a larger part of the target taxpayer's return information in certain whistleblower appeals.
events.quote: the USTC opinion in the case Whistleblower 972-17W v. Commissioner, 159 T.C. No. 1 (2022)

events.title: Publication 5251 (claim process) updated
events.description: The IRS updates Publication 5251, The Whistleblower Claim Process, clarifying information on the programme.
events.quote: The IRS updated Publication 5251 (The Whistleblower Claim Process) in September 2022

events.title: Bribery scheme to manipulate the IRS whistleblower programme; two arrested
events.description: In FY2023 an FBI/TIGTA criminal investigation, assisted by the Whistleblower Office, into matters including an attempt to manipulate the IRS whistleblower programme led to the arrest of two external individuals (not named in the report; date within FY2023 not given).
events.location: PDF p. 7, Assistance with Bribery Investigation
events.quote: The investigation, conducted by the FBI and TIGTA, resulted in the arrest of two external individuals.

events.title: 90-day target for status-and-stage letters
events.description: The Whistleblower Office sets a target of issuing Taxpayer First Act status-and-stage notices within 90 days of a written request.
events.quote: Effective July 31, 2023, the Whistleblower Office established a target timeframe to issue the Status and Stage notice within 90 days

events.title: IRS news release links the Whistleblower Office to ESOP compliance issues
events.description: IR-2023-144 cautions plan sponsors about employee stock ownership plan compliance; the first IRS notice to tie the Whistleblower Office to a specific issue the IRS wants to pursue.
events.quote: On August 9, 2023, IR-2023-144 was issued to caution plan sponsors to be alert to ESOP compliance issues.

events.title: Whistleblower Office expands to 84 staff and takes back the intake team
events.description: During FY2024 (Oct 2023-Sep 2024) the office restructured, grew from 49 to 84 full-time employees (partly by realigning the Initial Claim Evaluation team from SB/SE) and secured funding for a new claim system and online submission portal.
events.quote: In FY 2024, the Whistleblower Office expanded from 49 to 84 full-time employees and restructured the office

events.title: Whistleblower project in Treasury-IRS 2024-2025 Priority Guidance Plan
events.description: The initial 2024-2025 Priority Guidance Plan includes a project on the IRS whistleblower programme.
events.location: PDF p. 16, Inclusion in the Treasury Department's 2024-2025 Priority Guidance Plan
events.quote: The IRS Whistleblower Program has a project included in the initial version of the Priority Guidance Plan for 2024-2025.

events.title: Informant claims processing consolidated at Ogden
events.description: Informant claims operations formerly at five IRS campuses are consolidated in the Ogden Informant Claims Examination unit in FY2006, completed in FY2007.
events.quote: Informant claims operations formerly assigned to five IRS Campuses were consolidated at the Ogden Informant Claims Examination (ICE) unit in FY 2006.

new_indicators.name: Share of tips in a category
new_indicators.definition: Share of the tips, submissions or claims a programme received that fall in a category (e.g. not meeting a legal threshold, anonymous, from abroad), as printed by the source; breakdown item= says which.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-whistleblowing-usa7 (IRS FY2010 report: about 85 percent of submissions do not meet the 7623(b) thresholds).

new_indicators.name: Days open claims have spent in their current status
new_indicators.definition: For claims still open at a date, the average, longest or shortest number of days spent in their current processing status (breakdown item= gives the status, stat= the measure), as printed by the source. Not the time to an award.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-whistleblowing-usa7 (IRS annual reports FY2011-FY2013, tables of days in current status for open 7623(b) claims).

new_indicators.name: Preliminary award recommendation letters issued
new_indicators.definition: Preliminary award recommendation letters (or similar preliminary award determinations) a programme issued to whistleblowers in a period, as counted by the source; a count, not money.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-whistleblowing-usa7 (IRS FY2018 report: 268 PARLs issued; awards_accrued is for money).

new_indicators.name: Status notices sent to whistleblowers
new_indicators.definition: Notices or letters a programme sent to whistleblowers about the progress of their claim in a period (e.g. IRS Taxpayer First Act notices: referral for audit, payment of tax, status and stage letters); breakdown item= says which.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-whistleblowing-usa7 (IRS FY2021-FY2024 reports, Taxpayer First Act disclosure tables). The referral notices already in the data are filed under claims_referred_to_exam item=tfa_referral_notices; the main session may move them here.

ledger.contains: IRS Whistleblower Program FY2010 report to Congress (20 pp., Rev. 6-2011): program history and rules (pre-2006 discretionary policy of 1/10/15 percent and $10 million cap; 7623(b) 15-30 percent, 10 percent for public-source cases, $2 million and $200,000 thresholds; 30-day Tax Court appeal); IRM revision June 2010 (7623(a) claims from 1 July 2010 on 7623(b) percentages); case management system; staffing (17, increase to 21 authorised; staff counts not recorded, no indicator); 7623(b) submissions and taxpayers FY2007-2010 (Table 1); administrative priorities and legislative issues (about 85 percent of submissions below the 7623(b) thresholds); Table 2 7623(a) cases received, awards paid, paid claims with collections over $2 million, award amounts and collections FY2006-2010 (title says FY2005-2010 but FY2005 is not printed); 17 partial payments totalling $13 million; appendix reprinting section 7623. Added: the "collections over $2 million" row, the partial-payment count, the 85 percent share (proposed indicator tips_share), restated rules and three events. Everything else was already in the data.

One-page IRS notice: award payments under section 7623 made in FY2025 are reduced by the FY2025 sequestration rate of 5.7%, whatever the Form 211 date (Budget Control Act 2011 as amended). The rate is already recorded as a rule; nothing else in scope. The file is named fy-2026-sequester-notice.pdf but states the FY2025 rate.

NHTSA press release, 9 Nov 2021 (Wayback copy): first whistleblower award, more than $24 million, the legal maximum of the $81 million collected in cash from Hyundai and Kia; November 2020 consent orders over untimely recalls of over 1.6 million Theta II vehicles, combined penalties $210 million; statutory maximum 30 percent and $1 million threshold; contact details; webpage launched earlier in 2021. The case and the event were already recorded (twice each from this source: cases c-2fe1a61a52 and c-acde6dec05, events e-c85947ecd9 and e-2dcf91fe11, apparently duplicates). Added the two rules. The recall count (1.6 million vehicles) is out of scope.

Redacted NHTSA order determining whistleblower award request No. 2021-0001 (10 pp., undated in the text layer): statutory framework (10-30 percent of collected sanctions over $1 million, discretion); Requestor One, a former Hyundai Motor Company employee in South Korea, first came to NHTSA in August 2016; investigations RQ17-003/004 opened 18 May 2017; consent orders of 23 Nov 2020 with Non-Deferred ($54m Hyundai, $27m Kia, paid January 2021), Abeyance ($46m, $27m) and Performance Obligation ($40m, $16m) amounts, $210 million in total; award of $24,300,000 = 30 percent of the $81 million collected, plus 30 percent of any Performance Obligation Amount collected later, decision on Abeyance Amounts reserved; the whistleblower's request for $41.1 million (30 percent of $137 million, about 51 percent of the amount collected) rejected; NHTSA's reading that at least 70 percent of penalties go to the Highway Trust Fund. The case was already recorded (c-ae2e194951) but without sanctions_amount: the order gives $81 million collected (correction suggested, not a new case row). Added collections and ordered sanctions by component (parts add to 81 and 210 million), four restated rules and two events. The order itself is anonymous ("Requestor One"); the existing case row names the whistleblower from other sources (he went public).

Federal Register final rule 89 FR 101952 (17 Dec 2024, 42 pp.) creating 49 CFR Part 513, effective 16 Jan 2025: background and discussion of the 14 comments received on the 2023 proposal; definitions (covered action, original information, whistleblower); submission procedure and forms WB-INFO, WB-RELEASE, WB-AWARD (anonymous filing through a legal representative); confidentiality; ineligibility; Notice of Covered Action and 90-day claim window; award determination factors; award range 10-30 percent of collected sanctions over $1,000,000; 30-day appeal; regulatory analyses with Paperwork Reduction Act estimates (about 300 submissions since 2015 already recorded; projected about 50 WB-INFO filers, 45 WB-RELEASE forms, 1-2 Notices and about 2 WB-AWARD forms a year; burden hours and costs, out of scope); text of the forms. Last page holds the start of an unrelated NOAA rule. Added the three projections, four rules (10/30 percent, $1 million threshold, 30-day appeal). The count of comments (14) and form burden figures are out of scope.

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2011 report to Congress (21 pp., Rev. 6-2012): program history and rules (as FY2010); staffing (18 at year end, out of scope); case management and the August 2011 GAO review; guidance (IRM 2010, collected-proceeds regulation: proposed Jan 2011, hearing May 2011, final 22 Feb 2012; 6103(n) contract regulations effective 15 Mar 2011); first 7623(b) awards paid in FY2011 (too few to report separately); 7623(b) submissions and taxpayers FY2007-2011 (Table 1); open 7623(b) claims by status with submissions, taxpayers, whistleblowers and claims (Table 2, parts add to totals); days in current status (Table 3); administrative priorities and legislative issues (FBAR penalties not usable for awards; 85 percent of submissions below thresholds); Table 4 cases received, awards paid, paid claims with collections over $2 million, award amounts, collections and awards as a percentage of collections FY2007-2011; no partial payments in FY2011 (words, not recorded); appendix reprinting section 7623. Added the full Table 2 and Table 3, the over-$2-million and percentage rows of Table 4, the 85 percent share, restated rules and four events.

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2012 report to Congress (24 pp.): program history and rules; staffing (18 at start, ICE unit of 13 transferred January 2012, 36 at year end; staff counts out of scope); case management changes July-August 2012; guidance (collected-proceeds regulations 22 Feb 2012, interim guidance 7 Jun 2012, Deputy Commissioner memo 20 Jun 2012, proposed regulations 18 Dec 2012); five 7623(b) claims paid since FY2011 and the $104 million award of 27 Aug 2012 (both already recorded); 7623(b) submissions FY2007-2012 (Table 1, already recorded); open 7623(b) claims by status incl. four new suspended sub-statuses as of 10 Dec 2012 (Table 2, parts add to totals); days in current status (Table 3); intake change for FY2013 (SB/SE about 5 percent potential 7623(b), LB&I about two thirds); legislative issues; Table 4 FY2008-2012 cases received, awards paid, collections over $2 million, award amounts, collections, awards as percentage of collections; four partial payments in FY2012. Added Table 2 and 3 in full, the over-$2-million and percentage rows, partial-payment count, the SB/SE share, restated rules and four events. The note that new suspension reasons were applied to about 23 percent of suspended claims (data-recording progress) is not recorded.

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2013 report to Congress (24 pp., Rev. 4-2014): program history and rules; staffing (36 at start, 39 at year end; out of scope); proposed regulations (Dec 2012, hearing 10 Apr 2013); nine 7623(b) awards since FY2011; 122 awards totalling $55 million (table $53,054,302) and the 8.7 percent sequestration ($464,706); legislative issues (FY2014 Budget proposals); appendix reprinting section 7623; Table 1 claims received and open by fiscal year of receipt (pre-2007 to 2013); Table 2 FY2013 receipts by operating division and potential claim type (submissions and claims); Table 3 FY2013 closures by reason and year of receipt (78 percent closed in year of receipt or next); Table 4 open potential-7623(b) claims by status as of 6 Mar 2014; Table 5 days in current status; Table 6 awards, collections over $2 million, amounts and percentages FY2009-2013. Added: Table 1 grand total (year columns add to 51,300, printed 51,390), Table 2 by division, Table 3 by year of receipt, Tables 4 and 5 in full, over-$2-million and percentage rows of Table 6, the 78 percent share, restated rules and two events.

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2014 report to Congress (24 pp.): executive summary (record 14,365 claims; 101 awards totalling $52,281,628 before a $3,764,722 sequestration cut, 16.9 percent of collections); program history and rules; final regulations 12 Aug 2014 and Deputy Commissioner memo 20 Aug 2014 (events already recorded); eleven 7623(b) payments since FY2011; staffing (40 to 43, out of scope); legislative proposals; Appendix A statute; Table 1 claims received and open by year of receipt (pre-2010 to 2014, as of 14 May 2015); Table 2 FY2014 receipts by operating division and claim type; Table 3 FY2014 closures by reason and year of receipt (80 percent received in FY2013-14); Table 4 open potential-7623(b) claims by 21 statuses; Table 5 days in status; Table 6 awards FY2010-2014 incl. collections over $2 million and percentages. The rise of 3,845 claims on FY2013 is a difference and is not recorded. Note: Table 6 award amounts are before sequestration (the FY2014 rows already in the data carry no before_sequestration flag).

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2015 report to Congress (18 pp., Rev. 2-2016), first on a three-fiscal-year basis: Director's message (cumulative $403 million awarded on over $3 billion collected; claims received down 17 percent and closures up 27 percent, changes not recorded); background and rules; 19 award payments involving 49 7623(b) claims; staffing and Figure 1 FTEs by unit FY2013-2015 (out of scope); program review; legislative proposals; Table 1 awards, claims related to paid awards, collections over $2 million, amounts and percentages FY2013-2015 (pre-sequestration); Figure 2 claims paid and average days/years to process by claim type; Figure 3 FY2015 claims received by month and type (stand-alone, master, related); Figure 4 claims received, open, closed FY2013-2015; Table 2 open claims by processing phase and claim type at 30 Sep 2015; Table 3 FY2015 closures by reason with percentages (79 percent from FY2014-15 receipts; Closed-Other down 24 percent, not recorded); glossary. Everything else was already in the data.
